newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products revive with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products revive with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices revived late on Wednesday, with buyers again in the market after the morning's downturn briefly drew them to the sidelines.
"It's just higher crude prices," one broker said, referring to the moderate rises in West Coast products.
NYMEX crude oil for November delivery ended 39 cents higher at $24.46 a barrel. Heating oil touched post-Gulf War highs.
Conventional regular gasoline in Los Angeles rose one cent to 67/68 cents a gallon after idling earlier. San Francisco grades were priced about 2.75 cents lower.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles rebounded 1.50 cents to 72.50/73.50 cents a gallon, with a deal heard done at 73 cents.
CARB diesel in L.A. rose two cents to 74/75 cents a gallon.

Bids for low-sulphur or "EPA" diesel in L.A. held onto earlier gains at 71.50/73 cents. EPA rose early on talk that a major Californian nuclear plant needed diesel fuel to run backup generators after a shutdown on Tuesday.
